title: Impact Slices — personal KPI & learning notebook
content:
Context:
- Personal two-week sprint notebook focused on 'impact slices' — small measurable changes that should move a primary metric for my area (inference tail latency and cost/unit).
- This is informal: capture riffs, quick experiments, outcomes, and questions to bring into 1:1 and the weekly sync.

Primary metric (north star for next 2 weeks):
- Reduce hot-route p95 latency from current ~210ms -> target 170ms (client-facing text-gen route under < 512 tokens).
- Why this matters: reduces user-block timeouts and reduces fallback invocations which cascade into cost and poor UX.

Secondary metrics (guardrails & co-benefits):
- Median latency target: <= 90ms
- Cache hit ratio for prefix/KV caching: current 14% -> target 30%
- Cost per 1k tokens on this route: track weekly baseline (currently est $2.8/1k)
- Error rate (5xx): remain < 0.5%

Hypotheses (H1–H4):
- H1: Enabling small windowed batching (max batch 8, max latency 12ms) will reduce p95 by ~20–30ms for our workload distribution without increasing median much.
- H2: A conservative KV prefix cache for top-10 prompt templates increases cache hit and decreases token work for repeated flows (expect 12–18% latency improvement on cached requests).
- H3: Switching one model shard to int8 quantized weights reduces per-token CPU time and slightly improves tail variance for short sequences. Risk: quality drift on rare templates.
- H4: Route-based SmartRouting (prefer local region + dedicated small pool) reduces cross-region variance, improving p95 by 10–15ms for affected subset.

Planned micro-experiments (2-week cadence):
1) Batch policy A/B (Week A: adaptive batching 12ms cap, Week B: current baseline). Instrument tagging and run for 3 full days. (JIRA INF-2247)
2) KV cache pilot on /generate-chat route: implement with 60s TTL, monitor hitrate and evictions. Quick rollback plan if hallucination/regression spikes.
3) Quantize dev model variant using new quant profile (q8) for internal canary. Run eval set of 120 prompts used by the product team.
4) SmartRouting rule: test routing 20% of traffic to same-region dedicated micro-pool (auto-fallback enabled).

Week 1 — quick notes (first 5 days):
- Day 1: Baseline capture complete. p95 = 209–215ms depending on period. Median 95ms.
- Day 2: Deployed lightweight batching (policy A). Observed median unchanged, p95 dropped ~18ms during 09:00–11:00 PST peak. Logging noise: a handful of reroutes triggered fallback.
- Day 3: KV cache prototype integrated into dev environment. Hit rate ~16% on synthetic replay. Need to tune key derivation (current keys too specific).
- Day 4: Quantized canary built (q8). Internal eval shows BLEU-like metrics unchanged for common prompts; one outlier prompt shows slight wording truncation.
- Day 5: Quick analysis: batching + prefix caching together may be additive; need combined test. Raised PR #314 for batching telemetry changes.

Week 1 action items (todo):
- Short: add request metadata tags for canary traffic (me)
- Short: adjust KV key normalization to remove volatile tokens (ticket: INF-2251)
- Short: add fallback reason logging to correlated traces (instrument in tracing agent)
- Blocker: need a replay dataset with redwood-realistic distribution (ask data infra)

Week 2 — plan (what I want to run):
- Combined test: batching policy A + KV cache enabled on 10% production-simulated traffic in dev cluster. Measure additive effects and examine any quality regressions.
- Run quantized canary through the product eval harness (120 prompts) and run the new eval diff-alert to see if any regressions exceed threshold.
- Launch SmartRouting micro-pool at 5% traffic and monitor p95 and fallback counts.

Retrospective template (for end of week 2):
- What moved the needle most? (numeric)
- Observed regressions or customer-impact signals?
- What assumptions were wrong?
- Next 2-week focused slice (one bold change + observation plan)
- People to sync with / follow-ups (names + channels)

Quick wins to try if blocked: 
- Reduce model max tokens for ephemeral user queries to 384 (saves average token units). A/B on cost per response.
- Flip cache TTL to 30s to surface more misses and iterate key schema quickly.

Open questions / blockers: 
- Replay dataset: who owns? (ping @data-platform) — need representative user traces, including long-tail prompts.
- Approval flow for running quantized variant on staging: need sign-off from applied-ml.
- Can smart-routing be toggled per customer for targeted experiments without infra churn?

Notes to self / 1:1 talking points:
- Ask for 2 extra GPU-hours on dev pool to run quant canary overnight.
- Share early numbers with product (Evelyn) before any routing changes.
- Document the key derivation decision in confluence (link in linked_artifacts).

Random observations / noise (scratch):
- Noticed a spike in 5xx when KV cache miss rate goes >70% — probably bug in serialization path. Put quick monitor alert.
- Users hitting the route from APAC show 30ms higher p95 — might be region network or model shard location.

Final quick checklist before next sync:
- [ ] Combine batching + kv cache in dev replay
- [ ] Push PR #314 to staging with extra telemetry
- [ ] Run eval suite for quantized variant and record diffs
- [ ] Book 1:1 with Evelyn for tradeoff discussion

End of notebook entry — keep this doc as the working ground truth for the next two weeks.

(If this matures, move to a more formal weekly-report doc in shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime.)
